entities.summary:
The Battle of the Zab was a pivotal conflict in 750 CE that took place in the Great Zab region of Iraq. It was a defining moment in the Arab conquest of the Middle East, marking a decisive victory for the Abbasid Caliphate over the Byzantine Empire. The battle's significance extends beyond the region, as it contributed to the spread of Islam and the establishment of a new world order.

The core events surrounding the Battle of the Zab involved a series of skirmishes and battles between Arab and Byzantine forces, resulting in the eventual defeat of the Byzantine army. This victory had far-reaching consequences, including the expansion of Arab territories and the establishment of a new Islamic dynasty.

The legacy of the Battle of the Zab can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Abbasid Caliphate, which went on to become a major center of learning and culture in the Islamic world. The battle's impact also extended to the Byzantine Empire, which was weakened by the loss and eventually succumbed to the Arab conquest.

As the Arab historian Ibn al-Athir wrote, 'The victory of the Arabs in the Battle of the Zab was a turning point in the history of the Middle East, marking the beginning of a new era of Arab dominance.'
